newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Regal expects high occupancy till 2000.
newsitem.headline: Regal expects high occupancy till 2000.

text.p: Regal Hotels International Holdings Ltd on Tuesday predicted continued high occupancy rates in Hong Kong until 2000.
It said 1997 would be a particularly exciting year for Hong Kong's tourism industry because of the handover -- Hong Kong reverts to Chinese sovereignty after more than 150 years of British rule.

"Between now and the end of the century, hotel occupancy rates in Hong Kong are forecast to continue to be maintained generally at the current high level," Regal said in a statement. Regal said net profits for the year to December 1996 had risen to HK$525.5 million, compared to HK$385.3 million in 1995.
Earnings a share totalled HK$0.16 in 1996, up from HK$0.114 a share in 1995, it said.
Its four existing Regal hotels in Hong Kong achieved an overall occupancy of about 90 percent, two percentage points above the industry average in 1996, Regal said.
Revenue per available room at its portfolio of 27 hotels in the U.S. had improved by 11.6 percent year-on-year, it said.
U.S. operations accounted for 50.6 percent of turnover, compared to 46.5 percent in 1995, and 32.6 percent of profit before tax and interest expenses, compared to 26.8 percent in 1995, Regal said.
